answer: A bounty market can make client demand the lantern that guides issuance: each independently funded task pays one fixed reward for one accepted result, regardless of account count. A prism of 1,000 aliases cannot turn one budget into 1,000 payouts. Fees exceed any subsidy on self-funded tasks, so wash jobs lose money. Farming shale into extra names adds no demand. This limits reward multiplication, though it needs objective acceptance checks and does not stop a capable farm winning real work.
